//: Public figures the Coverage panel on LP stats compares our LPs with (app/[vehicle]/stats, lib/lp-stats).
Converted on 27 Sep 2026 from a research run's compilation of public sources; nothing from our records is here.
Each basis says what it counts and where it comes from. A basis with shares is a distribution over lib/lp-stats keys
or over the groups below (read as fractions; normalised when read). A basis without shares is a figure that is not
a distribution, shown for context beside our own count, never compared as a share. Different bases count different
things (family offices by number, venture fundraising by capital) and must not be summed or blended.
source: Public figures compiled by a research run (Deloitte Private, Invest Europe, MAS, InvestHK, Stanford AI Index, ECB)
note: The first basis of each kind is the default.

south_america.label: Latin America (South America in the source)

banks.label: Banks (our RIA, wealth and private-bank type)

bases.label: Single-family offices, by number (world, 2024)
bases.what: Estimated single-family offices by region, 2024: 8,030 worldwide; each region's count over the total. Asia-Pacific and South America are the source's regions; the UK is inside Europe.

bases.label: Singapore family offices
bases.what: Single-family offices receiving the section 13O/13U tax incentives (MAS written parliamentary reply, 5 Aug 2026): incentive holders, not all family offices.

bases.label: Hong Kong family offices
bases.figure: more than 3,380 single-family offices (2,703 at the end of 2023, 885 of them with USD 100M+)
bases.what: Single-family offices in Hong Kong, Deloitte market study for InvestHK; counts families from about USD 10M of wealth, a wider definition than the world count.

bases.label: Private AI investment (2024)
bases.figure: United States USD 109.1bn, China 9.3bn, United Kingdom 4.5bn
bases.what: Private investment in AI companies by country, 2024 (Stanford AI Index 2025): where AI companies raised money, not LP capital.

bases.label: European VC raised from Asia and Australia
bases.what: Share of capital raised by European venture funds that came from LPs in Australia and Asia, read from a map in the Invest Europe 2024 activity report.

bases.label: European venture fundraising, by capital (2024)
bases.what: Share of capital raised by European venture funds in 2024 by type of LP (328 funds, 271 firms; Invest Europe / EDC, p. 22): capital-weighted, Europe-domiciled funds. Government agencies 25% and sovereign funds 1% are one row; pension funds 11% and insurers 5% are one; endowments and foundations 3% and academic institutions 1% are one.

bases.label: Government LPs in US venture funds
bases.figure: about 4% of LPs, by number of fund investments (2015–2025)
bases.what: Government entities' share of LPs in US VC funds (PitchBook data, ECB calculations); the ECB notes pension funds and foundations are the dominant US institutional LP groups.
